blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Working across the four nations of the UK means respecting that, although everyone speaks English, business cultures differ in small but important ways. A meeting in Edinburgh feels different from one in London; one in Cardiff may be warmer and more direct; Belfast has its own pace and humour.

Accents matter more than you think. A Glasgow accent is not a London accent, and assuming a Scot will 'sound English' is a quick way to get a cold welcome. Learn the names of the regions, listen to the voices, and never use 'England' when you mean 'the UK'.

The best cross-national British teams treat regional differences as a strength. Jokes are made gently on both sides — but the respect underneath is never optional.

items.q: According to the text, what do the four nations share, and what differs?
options: They share the same business culture, but their language differs
They share the language, but their business cultures differ
They share the same accent, but their laws differ
items.why: "although everyone speaks English, business cultures differ in small but important ways".

items.q: How does the text describe a meeting in Cardiff?
items.why: "one in Cardiff may be warmer and more direct".

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which statement?
options: Respect should sit underneath any joke
'England' and 'the UK' can be used interchangeably
Regional differences can be an asset for a team
Accents carry real meaning in business relationships
items.why: Inferência: o texto diz explicitamente para nunca usar 'England' querendo dizer 'the UK'.

items.q: What does the phrase "a quick way to get a cold welcome" suggest?
options: Scots dislike all visitors from London
Misjudging someone's accent can damage the first impression
Meetings in Scotland always start badly
The weather in Glasgow is unpleasant
items.why: Inferência: presumir que um escocês 'soa inglês' cria uma recepção fria — ou seja, prejudica o relacionamento inicial.

items.q: What does the text imply about jokes between the nations?
options: They replace the need for real respect
They only work in one direction
They are acceptable as long as respect remains underneath
items.why: Inferência: "Jokes are made gently on both sides — but the respect underneath is never optional."

blocks.instruction: Ouça Harry orientando a equipe. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Right, before the Manchester office opens next month, I want to flag a few things — small on paper, but they matter to the clients in Scotland and Wales.

First, the accents. The team here in Manchester will spend a lot of time on calls with Glasgow and Edinburgh. Please don't treat every British voice as the same. A Glasgow accent is not a London accent, and if you assume a Scottish client will 'sound English', you'll get a very cold welcome — I've watched it happen.

Second, and I can't stress this enough: never say 'England' when you mean 'the UK'. Our client in Cardiff is Welsh, not English, and that slip lands badly. It sounds careless, and it undoes a lot of goodwill.

Now, the tone. Belfast has its own pace and humour, and Cardiff tends to be warmer and more direct than London. None of that is a problem — it's a strength, honestly, once you tune into it. Listen first, learn the names of the regions, and let the relationship build.

The jokes will come, on both sides, and that's fine. But keep them gentle. The respect underneath is never optional. Any questions before we set the call schedule?
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: Why is Harry giving this briefing now?
options: Because a client complained about a delivery
Because the Scottish office is closing
Because the Manchester office is about to open and clients are in Scotland and Wales
Because the team failed an audit
items.why: "before the Manchester office opens next month… clients in Scotland and Wales."

items.q: What does Harry say about assuming a Scottish client will 'sound English'?
options: It leads to a very cold welcome
items.why: "if you assume a Scottish client will 'sound English', you'll get a very cold welcome."

items.q: Why does Harry warn against saying 'England' when you mean 'the UK'?
options: It sounds careless and undoes goodwill with clients like the one in Cardiff
It is too formal for calls
items.why: "It sounds careless, and it undoes a lot of goodwill" — o cliente de Cardiff é galês, não inglês.

items.q: When Harry says regional differences are "a strength… once you tune into it", he implies that…
options: only Manchester staff can understand them
the differences should be removed over time
the differences slow every project down
the team must first learn to notice and respect them before they help
items.why: Inferência: a diferença só vira força depois que a equipe 'sintoniza' — aprende a percebê-la e respeitá-la.

items.q: How would you best describe Harry's overall attitude in the briefing?
options: Purely focused on the call schedule
Anxious that the office should not open
Practical and respectful, treating the differences as manageable
items.why: Inferência: ele dá avisos concretos, mas chama as diferenças de 'força' e propõe um caminho — tom prático e respeitoso.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "They work well as a cross-national team, spanning Scotland, Wales and England." Cross-national means…
options: led by a single national office
items.why: Cross-national = entre nações: envolve mais de uma nação trabalhando junta.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "His strong Glasgow ___ made some colleagues assume, wrongly, that he was hard to understand."
items.why: Accent = sotaque, o traço de pronúncia associado a Glasgow.

items.q: "Getting the client's nation wrong earned the rep a cold welcome." A cold welcome is…
items.why: Cold welcome = recepção fria, pouco acolhedora.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Instead of a weakness, the mix of regional styles became the team's greatest ___."
items.why: Strength = força, ponto forte — o oposto de weakness.

items.q: "He corrected the mistake gently, so nobody felt embarrassed." Gently means…
items.why: Gently = gentilmente, de forma suave e cuidadosa.

blocks.instruction: Expressões e phrasal verbs que aparecem em times que trabalham entre as nações. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "It takes a while to tune into the humour in Belfast." To tune into something means to…
options: become sensitive to it and understand it
items.why: Tune into = sintonizar, passar a perceber e entender algo.

items.q: "Before the launch we need to iron out the differences in how each office runs meetings." To iron out means to…
items.why: Iron out = resolver, eliminar pequenos problemas ou atritos.

items.q: "The Cardiff client called out our slip when we said 'England' instead of 'the UK'." To call out something means to…
options: point it out and challenge it openly
items.why: Call out = apontar e questionar abertamente um erro ou comportamento.

items.q: "Let's build on the trust we've earned in Scotland before we approach Wales." To build on something means to…
options: use it as a base to develop further
items.why: Build on = construir sobre, usar algo já conquistado como base para avançar.

items.q: "Take time to get to grips with the regional names before your first call." To get to grips with means to…
options: begin to understand and handle properly
items.why: Get to grips with = começar a dominar, entender e lidar corretamente com algo.
